headlines.title: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Stock Still Looks Overvalued Despite AI Chip Demand
headlines.summary: Cadence Design Systems stock has pulled back in recent months, yet the latest valuation checks still point to a rich price tag, with both the market multiple view and an intrinsic value estimate suggesting the shares trade at a premium. At the same time, the company continues to push its technology forward in areas such as PCIe 6.0, which helps explain why investors are willing to pay up. Over the past 5 years Cadence Design Systems has delivered a total return of 75.

headlines.title: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Following PCIe 6.0 Progress Has Fair Value Back In Focus
headlines.summary: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) recently reported first pass compliance for its PCIe 6.0 PHY and controller IP on TSMC’s N3 process, which has put a fresh spotlight on the stock after a weaker year of returns. Despite the PCIe 6.0 milestone, Cadence Design Systems’ recent share price performance has been weak, with the stock down 22.19% over 90 days and 13.16% over 30 days. The 1-year total shareholder return of 16.61% contrasts with longer term gains of 22.99% over three years and 75.

headlines.title: What Sets Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Apart After Its PCIe 6.0 Milestone?
headlines.summary: Cadence Design Systems (NasdaqGS: CDNS) reported that its PCIe 6.0 subsystem achieved first pass compliance at an official PCI-SIG workshop and is now listed on the PCI-SIG Integrators List. The production ready subsystem targets high bandwidth connectivity needs in AI and high performance computing markets. The compliance result extends Cadence's technology offering from AI chip design tools to advanced interconnect subsystems aligned with the PCI Express 6.0 specification.

headlines.title: How Is Cadence Design Systems’ Stock Performance Compared to Other Application Software Stocks
headlines.summary: CDNS has underperformed the broader market over the past year, while analysts remain highly bullish on its future prospects.

description: Cadence Design Systems, Inc. develops computational, AI-driven software, hardware, and silicon intellectual property products and solutions. The company offers functional verification services, such as Jasper, a formal verification platform; Xcelium, a parallel logic simulation platform; Verisium, a generative AI solution; Palladium, an enterprise emulation platform; and Protium, a prototyping platform for chip verification, as well as digital IC design and sign off products, including In novus platform; and custom IC design and simulation product include Virtuoso, a platform to design and verify analog. It also provides Xcelium logic simulator and other front-end verification and virtual prototyping technologies; controllers and physical interfaces; PCI Express, universal accelerator and compute express links, and multiple memory interfaces; and Ten Silica, a digital signal processor. In addition, the company's design IP portfolio includes serializer/deserializer, peripheral component interconnect, USB, and other standard protocols; and Secure-IC, a solution for embedded security IP. Additionally, it provides System Design and Analysis (SD&A) platform, a solution that enables end-to-end system-level design and verification across chips, packages, PCBs, and electronic systems; Allegro X and Orca X platforms for PCB and advanced packaging; Sigrity X for signal and power integrity; AIR for RF design; Fidelity for computational fluid dynamics; Celsius for thermal and airflow analysis; Clarity 3D solver for electromagnetic and power electronics analysis and simulation; Integrity 3D-IC solution for 3D-IC and multi-chiplet designs; the Optimality Intelligent System Explorer, Reality digital twin, and Millennium enterprise multiphasic platforms; Allegro system design platform; and molecular modeling and simulation solutions and services. The company has a strategic collaboration with NVIDIA. The company was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
